survey: A stylized saguaro cactus on desert sand, seen in three-quarter view. The main trunk is a ribbed vertical column with a rounded top. Its base sinks into the sand, with a small sand rim and a contact shadow, so it is planted rather than floating. A pink flower sits on a small green bud at the crown and is attached to the trunk. The left arm leaves the lower-middle trunk, bends at an elbow and rises vertically. Its joint merges cleanly into the trunk silhouette. The right arm leaves the trunk higher up, on the near side, and curves up into a vertical tip. It overlaps the trunk in front with a clear, believable junction. Both arms have ribs that follow their curvature. Small yellow spines are scattered along the ribs of the trunk and arms, and a few poke out at the silhouette edges, which reads correctly as spines on the far side. Sparse single spines are an acceptable simplification of areole clusters. The rocks rest on the sand. Every part attaches where a real saguaro's would, with no floating, duplicated or invented parts.
